target_customer: Retail savers in France and Europe who want to accumulate bitcoin effortlessly
problem: Buying bitcoin is intimidating, so the app turns spare change and recurring buys into bitcoin and now adds a card and euro account.
business_model: Consumer fintech: trading fees, card interchange and subscription features

founders.name: Alexandre Roubaud
founders.background_notes: Led Product at Moka, acquired by Mogo (YC page)

technical_complexity.rationale: Custody, exchange and round-up integration under French crypto registration, plus card issuing through a partner.

defensibility.rationale: Regulatory registration helps, but features are copyable by exchanges and neobanks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not reached; no source on incumbent copies, and Bitstack obtained MiCA approval in 2025-06.

market_need_then: Growing retail interest in bitcoin and French registration regime for crypto providers (PSAN registration granted in 2022 per company).

branding.domain_note: bitstack-app.com, a suffixed domain; history not found.

identity.visual_style: Bitcoin orange themes likely but unconfirmed

branding.community_and_virality: Company claims 400,000 users and a 4.8 rating from 10,000 reviews; community equity raise with 8,000 investors (company claim).

brand_strength.rationale: Strong consumer traction and a crowd raise suggest some brand pull, but no independent brand coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: Bitstack grew from a spare-change bitcoin app to a licensed European bitcoin savings and card product, raising four institutional rounds ending with a $15M Series A in December 2025 and then a crowd round. Regulatory registration and MiCA approval gave a moat in France while the company expanded to four countries.
notes: Amounts for 2021 (EUR 1M), 2023 (EUR 2M) and 2024 (EUR 5M) come from company press release titles; recorded as null USD to avoid conversion. A third-party profile giving a $5.25M Series A led by ISAI looks unreliable. Crowd round amount stated by company and cryptoast and allnews.ch. Competitor list empty: only an undated Acorns reference and a 2015 US Lawnmower article were found, neither near the batch.
